t: Identify the phrase type: "HOLDING ONTO THE RIGGING FOR DEAR LIFE, I barely survived the storm."
e: This phrase gives context to the whole sentence without being grammatically tied to it, so it is an absolute phrase.

t: Identify the part of speech: "THIS is the unique problem."
e: 'This' is the subject of the sentence with no noun following it, so it is a pronoun.

t: Identify the clause type: "I cannot say WHEN HE COMES."
e: The clause is the object of 'say', so it is a noun clause.

t: Identify the Figure of Speech: "Parting is such sweet sorrow."
e: 'Sweet' and 'sorrow' are contradictory terms combined together.

t: Identify the clause type: "WHEN HE COMES, I will tell the truth."
e: The clause tells 'when' the main action happens, functioning as an adverb clause of time.

t: Identify the phrase type: "My father does not like MY GOING OUTSIDE."
e: 'Going outside' acts as a noun (object of 'like'), so it is a gerund phrase.

t: Identify the clause type: "I know the worker WHO IS DILIGENT."
e: The clause describes 'worker', functioning as an adjective clause.

t: Identify the Linking Verb usage: "He became an officer."
e: 'Became' can be replaced by 'was' without changing the core meaning, so it's a linking verb.

t: Identify the part of speech: "The meeting is OVER."
e: 'Over' describes the state of the subject 'meeting' (finished), functioning as an adjective.

t: Identify the part of speech: "I must EITHER work OR starve."
e: 'Either' joins two choices (work/starve) with 'or', functioning as a conjunction.

t: Identify the Verb type: "She got the first prize."
e: 'Got' here shows the action of winning/receiving, so it functions as an action verb, not linking.

t: Identify the phrase type: "Rohan, MY FRIEND, works hard."
e: 'My friend' renames 'Rohan', so it is an appositive phrase.

t: Identify the clause type: "I know WHAT YOU ARE SAYING."
e: The clause acts as the object of 'know', so it is a noun clause.

t: Identify the Word Formation: What is the noun form of "Receive"?
e: 'Receipt' is the standard noun form; 'receptive' is an adjective.

t: Identify the Word Formation: What is the noun form of "Evade"?
e: 'Evasion' is the noun; 'evasive' is the adjective form.

t: Identify the part of speech: "SOME girlfriends are very toxic."
e: 'Some' quantifies the noun 'girlfriends', so it is an adjective here.

t: Identify the Figure of Speech: "The wind whispered through the trees."
e: The wind (non-living) is given the human quality of whispering.

t: Identify the part of speech: "My beloved is PRETTY good in dancing."
e: 'Pretty' modifies the adjective 'good' (meaning 'quite'), so it functions as an adverb.

t: Find the error: "The sweet tasted deliciously."
e: 'Taste' as a linking verb takes an adjective, not an adverb → "tasted delicious."

t: Identify the part of speech: "None BUT the brave deserves the fair."
e: 'But' here means 'except', functioning as a preposition.

t: Identify the part of speech: "THIS house belongs to her."
e: 'This' precedes the noun 'house' and modifies it, so it is an adjective.

t: Identify the part of speech: "He fell OVER."
e: 'Over' modifies the verb 'fell' with no object, functioning as an adverb.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "Please come IN."
e: 'In' modifies the verb 'come' with no object following, so it functions as an adverb.

t: Identify the Word Formation: What is the adjective form of "Voice"?
e: 'Vocal' is the correct adjective form of 'Voice'.

t: Identify the Complement type: "We made him monitor."
e: 'Monitor' completes information about the object 'him', so it is an object complement.

t: Identify the clause type: "This is the time WHEN HE COMES."
e: The clause modifies the noun 'time', so it is an adjective clause.

t: Identify the phrase type: "A BURNING TRAIN was seen from a distance."
e: 'Burning' modifies the noun 'train' as an adjective, so it is a present participle phrase.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He runs FAST."
e: 'Fast' modifies the verb 'runs', telling how he runs — Adverb.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "She has a KIND heart."
e: 'Kind' describes the noun 'heart' — Adjective.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "WOW, what a goal!"
e: 'Wow' expresses sudden emotion, standing independently — Interjection.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He walked ACROSS the bridge."
e: 'Across' relates 'bridge' to the rest of the sentence, showing position — Preposition.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "EITHER you OR I am wrong."
e: 'Either...or' joins two alternatives — a correlative Conjunction.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "The FAST train left early."
e: Here 'fast' qualifies the noun 'train' — Adjective (same word, different POS by context).

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "HONESTY is the best policy."
e: 'Honesty' names a quality, not a tangible thing — Abstract Noun.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "This book is MINE."
e: 'Mine' stands alone in place of 'my book' — Possessive Pronoun (not followed by a noun).

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "This is MY book."
e: 'My' directly qualifies the noun 'book' — Possessive Adjective (determiner).

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He hurt HIMSELF while playing."
e: 'Himself' refers back to the subject and is essential to the meaning — Reflexive Pronoun.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "I MYSELF saw the accident."
e: 'Myself' here only adds emphasis and can be removed without changing meaning — Emphatic Pronoun.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "SOMEBODY left the door open."
e: 'Somebody' does not refer to any specific person — Indefinite Pronoun.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "The book, WHICH I bought yesterday, is interesting."
e: 'Which' relates back to 'book' and introduces a clause about it — Relative Pronoun.

t: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He works HARD to earn a living."
e: 'Hard' modifies the verb 'works', showing manner — Adverb.

t: Identify the phrase type: "READING BOOKS is his favourite hobby."
e: 'Reading books' acts as the subject and is built on a gerund (V-ing used as a noun) — Gerund Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "He wants TO WIN THE MATCH."
e: 'To win the match' begins with 'to + verb' functioning as the object — Infinitive Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "THE BOY IN THE BLUE SHIRT is my brother."
e: 'In the blue shirt' describes 'the boy' like an adjective — Adjective Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "SITTING BY THE WINDOW, she watched the rain."
e: 'Sitting by the window' modifies the subject 'she' as an adjective would — Participle Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "THE WEATHER BEING PLEASANT, we went for a walk."
e: This phrase has its own subject ('weather') and participle, independent of the main clause — Absolute Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "He lives IN A SMALL VILLAGE."
e: 'In a small village' begins with a preposition and shows place — Prepositional Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "He behaved IN A VERY RUDE MANNER."
e: 'In a very rude manner' modifies the verb 'behaved', telling how — Adverb Phrase (functioning as adverb).

t: Identify the phrase type: "THE OLD WOODEN HOUSE stood on the hill."
e: 'The old wooden house' is a group of words centred on the noun 'house', acting as subject — Noun Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "She HAS BEEN WORKING here since 2015."
e: 'Has been working' is a group of auxiliary + main verbs forming the predicate — Verb Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "EXHAUSTED FROM THE JOURNEY, he fell asleep instantly."
e: 'Exhausted from the journey' modifies 'he' and is built on a past participle — Participle Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "TO ERR is human, TO FORGIVE divine."
e: 'To err' and 'to forgive' function as subjects and begin with 'to + verb' — Infinitive Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "His main hobby is COLLECTING OLD COINS."
e: 'Collecting old coins' completes the subject complement using -ing as a noun — Gerund Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "The man STANDING AT THE GATE is a stranger."
e: 'Standing at the gate' describes 'the man' like an adjective — Participle Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "AFTER THE HEAVY RAIN, the roads were flooded."
e: 'After the heavy rain' tells when the roads were flooded, modifying the verb — Adverb Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "I saw A TALL DARK STRANGER at the door."
e: 'A tall dark stranger' is a group of words built around the noun 'stranger', used as the object — Noun Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "This is a matter OF GREAT IMPORTANCE."
e: 'Of great importance' begins with a preposition and describes 'matter' — Prepositional Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "He is EASY TO PLEASE."
e: 'To please' begins with 'to + verb', completing the adjective 'easy' — Infinitive Phrase.

t: Identify the phrase type: "TIRED AND HUNGRY, the travellers stopped at an inn."
e: 'Tired and hungry' is a group of adjectives describing 'the travellers' — Adjective Phrase.

t: Identify the clause type: "I know THAT HE IS HONEST."
e: 'That he is honest' is the object of 'know' — Noun Clause.

t: Identify the clause type: "This is the house WHERE I WAS BORN."
e: 'Where I was born' describes the noun 'house' — Adjective (Relative) Clause.

t: Identify the clause type: "WHEN THE BELL RANG, the students left."
e: 'When the bell rang' tells the time of the main action — Adverb Clause of Time.

t: Identify the clause type: "The boy WHO WON THE RACE is my friend."
e: 'Who won the race' describes 'the boy' — Adjective (Relative) Clause.

t: Identify the clause type: "WHAT HE SAID surprised everyone."
e: 'What he said' is the subject of the sentence — Noun Clause.

t: Identify the clause type: "She sang so well THAT EVERYONE APPLAUDED."
e: 'That everyone applauded' shows the result of 'so well' — Adverb Clause of Result.

t: Identify the clause type: "IF IT RAINS, we will stay indoors."
e: 'If it rains' states a condition for the main clause — Adverb Clause of Condition.

t: Identify the clause type: "AS HE WAS TIRED, he went to bed early."
e: 'As he was tired' gives the reason for going to bed early — Adverb Clause of Reason.

t: Identify the clause type: "He behaved AS IF HE WERE THE BOSS."
e: 'As if he were the boss' describes how he behaved — Adverb Clause of Manner.

t: Identify the clause type: "He is taller THAN HIS BROTHER IS."
e: 'Than his brother is' compares the degree of tallness — Adverb Clause of Comparison.

t: Identify the clause type: "I do not know WHY HE LEFT SO SOON."
e: 'Why he left so soon' is the object of 'know' — Noun Clause.

t: Identify the clause type: "Sit WHEREVER YOU LIKE."
e: 'Wherever you like' tells the place of sitting — Adverb Clause of Place.

t: Identify the clause type: "THOUGH HE IS RICH, he is not happy."
e: 'Though he is rich' shows a contrast/concession to the main clause — Adverb Clause of Concession.

t: Identify the clause type: "This is the reason WHY HE FAILED."
e: 'Why he failed' describes the noun 'reason' — Adjective Clause.

t: Identify the clause type: "He ran so fast THAT HE COULD NOT BE CAUGHT."
e: 'That he could not be caught' expresses the result of running fast — Adverb Clause of Result.

t: Identify the clause type in the sentence: "He said THAT HE WOULD COME."
e: 'That he would come' is the object of 'said' — Noun Clause.
